# Expo Universal App Architecture

## Core Principle: One Codebase, All Platforms

**Every application generated by the Design-First Software Factory is built with Expo to ensure universal accessibility across phones, tablets, and desktop browsers.**

## Why Expo (Not Generic React Native)

### The Problem with Generic React Native
- React Native alone targets iOS and Android (mobile only)
- Adding web support requires complex tooling (react-native-web)
- Managing three separate build pipelines is fragile
- No unified development experience

### The Expo Solution
- **Single codebase** → iOS, Android, and Web
- **Single development experience** → `expo start` runs everywhere
- **Single build system** → EAS Build handles all platforms
- **Progressive Web App (PWA)** → Desktop browser support built-in
- **Over-the-air updates** → Update apps without app store approval

## Universal Accessibility Requirements

### Every Generated App Must:
✅ **Run natively on iOS** (iPhone, iPad)
✅ **Run natively on Android** (phone, tablet)
✅ **Run as PWA on desktop web** (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge)
✅ **Be responsive** across screen sizes (phone, tablet, desktop)
✅ **Use platform-aware design** (iOS vs Android vs Web patterns)
✅ **Support offline capabilities** (PWA features)

### The Factory UI Must:
✅ **Be built with Expo** (not a traditional web app)
✅ **Optimized for desktop web** (complex workflows need screen real estate)
✅ **Also work on tablets** (for on-the-go management)
✅ **Use responsive design** (adapts to available space)

## Core Architecture Blueprint

### Directory Structure

```
my-expo-app/
├── src/                          # Shared codebase (all platforms)
│   ├── screens/                  # Screen components
│   ├── components/               # Reusable components
│   ├── services/                 # API and business logic
│   ├── navigation/               # Navigation setup
│   ├── theme/                    # Design tokens (platform-aware)
│   └── utils/                    # Utilities
├── platform-overrides/           # Platform-specific code (when needed)
│   ├── ios/                      # iOS-specific implementations
│   ├── android/                  # Android-specific implementations
│   └── web/                      # Web-specific implementations
├── app.json                      # Expo configuration
├── package.json                  # Dependencies
└── README.md                     # Setup instructions
```

### Platform-Aware Design Tokens

**DO NOT** use fixed values that don't adapt to platform:

```typescript
// ❌ BAD - Not platform-aware
export const spacing = {
  sm: 8,
  md: 16,
  lg: 24
};

export const colors = {
  primary: '#007AFF'  // iOS blue everywhere
};
```

**DO** use Platform.select for platform-specific values:

```typescript
// ✅ GOOD - Platform-aware
import { Platform } from 'react-native';

export const spacing = {
  xs: 4,
  sm: 8,
  md: 16,
  lg: 24,
  xl: Platform.select({
    ios: 32,
    android: 28,
    web: 48,  // More spacious on desktop
  }),
};

export const colors = {
  primary: Platform.select({
    ios: '#007AFF',        // iOS blue
    android: '#2196F3',    // Material blue
    web: '#0066CC',        // Web-optimized
  }),
  background: Platform.select({
    ios: '#F2F2F7',        // iOS light gray
    android: '#FFFFFF',    // Material white
    web: '#FAFAFA',        // Web subtle gray
  }),
};

export const typography = {
  fontSize: {
    body: Platform.select({
      ios: 17,
      android: 16,
      web: 16,
    }),
    heading: Platform.select({
      ios: 28,
      android: 24,
      web: 32,  // Larger on desktop
    }),
  },
  fontFamily: {
    regular: Platform.select({
      ios: 'System',
      android: 'Roboto',
      web: '-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif',
    }),
  },
};
```

### Platform-Specific Overrides

**When to use overrides**:
- Native modules (camera, location, push notifications)
- Platform-specific UI patterns (iOS swipe vs Android drawer)
- Web-specific features (SEO, document title, analytics)
- Performance optimizations per platform

**Example**:
```typescript
// src/services/analytics.ts
export * from './analytics.base';

// platform-overrides/ios/analytics.ts
import { Platform } from 'react-native';
import Analytics from '@react-native-firebase/analytics';

export const trackEvent = async (event: string, params: any) => {
  await Analytics().logEvent(event, params);
};

// platform-overrides/web/analytics.ts
export const trackEvent = async (event: string, params: any) => {
  if (typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.gtag) {
    window.gtag('event', event, params);
  }
};
```

**Build configuration** (metro.config.js):
```javascript
const { getDefaultConfig } = require('expo/metro-config');
const path = require('path');

const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);

// Add platform-overrides based on platform
const platform = process.env.EXPO_PLATFORM || 'ios';
const overridePath = path.resolve(__dirname, `platform-overrides/${platform}`);

config.resolver.extraNodeModules = {
  ...config.resolver.extraNodeModules,
  '@platform': overridePath,
};

module.exports = config;
```

## Responsive Design Strategy

### Mobile-First Approach

Always design for mobile first, then enhance for larger screens:

```typescript
import { useWindowDimensions } from 'react-native';

export function MyScreen() {
  const { width } = useWindowDimensions();

  const isPhone = width < 768;
  const isTablet = width >= 768 && width < 1024;
  const isDesktop = width >= 1024;

  return (
    <View style={{
      flexDirection: isPhone ? 'column' : 'row',
      padding: isPhone ? 16 : isTablet ? 24 : 32,
    }}>
      <View style={{ flex: isPhone ? 1 : 2 }}>
        {/* Main content */}
      </View>

      {!isPhone && (
        <View style={{ flex: 1 }}>
          {/* Sidebar - only on tablet/desktop */}
        </View>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}
```

### Breakpoint System

```typescript
export const breakpoints = {
  phone: 0,
  tablet: 768,
  desktop: 1024,
  wide: 1440,
};

export function useBreakpoint() {
  const { width } = useWindowDimensions();

  return {
    isPhone: width < breakpoints.tablet,
    isTablet: width >= breakpoints.tablet && width < breakpoints.desktop,
    isDesktop: width >= breakpoints.desktop,
    isWide: width >= breakpoints.wide,
  };
}
```

## Testing Strategy

### Testing Across Platforms

**Every generated app includes testing scaffolding**:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "test": "jest",
    "test:e2e:ios": "detox test --configuration ios.sim.debug",
    "test:e2e:android": "detox test --configuration android.emu.debug",
    "test:e2e:web": "playwright test"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "jest": "^29.0.0",
    "detox": "^20.0.0",
    "playwright": "^1.40.0",
    "@testing-library/react-native": "^12.0.0"
  }
}
```

**Test pyramid**:
1. **Unit tests** (Jest) - Business logic, utilities
2. **Component tests** (React Native Testing Library) - Individual components
3. **E2E tests** (Detox for mobile, Playwright for web) - Full user flows

### Mobile-Specific Testing

```typescript
// __tests__/LoginScreen.test.tsx
import { render, fireEvent } from '@testing-library/react-native';
import LoginScreen from '../src/screens/LoginScreen';

describe('LoginScreen', () => {
  it('should work on mobile', () => {
    const { getByTestId } = render(<LoginScreen />);

    fireEvent.changeText(getByTestId('email-input'), 'user@example.com');
    fireEvent.changeText(getByTestId('password-input'), 'password');
    fireEvent.press(getByTestId('login-button'));

    // Assertions...
  });
});
```

### E2E Testing Example (Detox)

```typescript
// e2e/login.e2e.ts
describe('Login Flow', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp();
  });

  it('should login successfully on iOS', async () => {
    await element(by.id('email-input')).typeText('user@example.com');
    await element(by.id('password-input')).typeText('password');
    await element(by.id('login-button')).tap();

    await expect(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

## Development Workflow

### Local Development

```bash
# Start development server (works for all platforms)
npx expo start

# Then choose platform:
# - Press 'i' for iOS simulator
# - Press 'a' for Android emulator
# - Press 'w' for web browser
```

### Platform-Specific Development

```bash
# iOS only
npx expo start --ios

# Android only
npx expo start --android

# Web only
npx expo start --web
```

### Building for Production

```bash
# iOS
eas build --platform ios --profile production

# Android
eas build --platform android --profile production

# Web
npx expo export:web
# Deploy to Vercel, Netlify, or any static host
```

## Progressive Web App (PWA) Configuration

### app.json Configuration

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "name": "My App",
    "slug": "my-app",
    "platforms": ["ios", "android", "web"],
    "web": {
      "favicon": "./assets/favicon.png",
      "bundler": "metro",
      "output": "static",
      "build": {
        "babel": {
          "include": ["@expo/vector-icons"]
        }
      }
    },
    "android": {
      "adaptiveIcon": {
        "foregroundImage": "./assets/adaptive-icon.png",
        "backgroundColor": "#FFFFFF"
      }
    },
    "ios": {
      "supportsTablet": true,
      "bundleIdentifier": "com.yourcompany.myapp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Web Manifest (Automatic)

Expo automatically generates a manifest.json for PWA:
- App icon
- Theme color
- Display mode
- Start URL
- Offline capabilities

### Service Worker (Expo Handles)

Expo automatically includes service worker for:
- Offline support
- App updates
- Asset caching

## Navigation Patterns

### Platform-Appropriate Navigation

```typescript
import { Platform } from 'react-native';
import { NavigationContainer } from '@react-navigation/native';
import { createNativeStackNavigator } from '@react-navigation/native-stack';
import { createBottomTabNavigator } from '@react-navigation/bottom-tabs';
import { createDrawerNavigator } from '@react-navigation/drawer';

const Stack = createNativeStackNavigator();
const Tab = createBottomTabNavigator();
const Drawer = createDrawerNavigator();

export function AppNavigator() {
  const isWeb = Platform.OS === 'web';
  const isPhone = !isWeb && Platform.OS !== 'macos';

  if (isWeb) {
    // Desktop web: Use drawer for navigation
    return (
      <NavigationContainer>
        <Drawer.Navigator>
          <Drawer.Screen name="Home" component={HomeScreen} />
          <Drawer.Screen name="Profile" component={ProfileScreen} />
        </Drawer.Navigator>
      </NavigationContainer>
    );
  }

  if (isPhone) {
    // Mobile: Use bottom tabs
    return (
      <NavigationContainer>
        <Tab.Navigator>
          <Tab.Screen name="Home" component={HomeScreen} />
          <Tab.Screen name="Profile" component={ProfileScreen} />
        </Tab.Navigator>
      </NavigationContainer>
    );
  }

  // Tablet: Use sidebar
  return (
    <NavigationContainer>
      <Drawer.Navigator
        screenOptions={{
          drawerType: 'permanent',
          drawerStyle: { width: 240 },
        }}
      >
        <Drawer.Screen name="Home" component={HomeScreen} />
        <Drawer.Screen name="Profile" component={ProfileScreen} />
      </Drawer.Navigator>
    </NavigationContainer>
  );
}
```

## Performance Optimization

### Web-Specific Optimizations

```typescript
// Lazy load heavy screens on web
import { lazy, Suspense } from 'react';
import { Platform } from 'react-native';

const DashboardScreen = Platform.OS === 'web'
  ? lazy(() => import('./screens/DashboardScreen'))
  : require('./screens/DashboardScreen').default;

export function App() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<LoadingScreen />}>
      <DashboardScreen />
    </Suspense>
  );
}
```

### Image Optimization

```typescript
import { Image, Platform } from 'react-native';

export function OptimizedImage({ source, ...props }) {
  // Use WebP on web for better compression
  const optimizedSource = Platform.OS === 'web'
    ? { uri: source.uri.replace('.png', '.webp') }
    : source;

  return <Image source={optimizedSource} {...props} />;
}
```

## Accessibility

### Cross-Platform Accessibility

```typescript
import { View, Text, TouchableOpacity, Platform } from 'react-native';

export function AccessibleButton({ label, onPress }) {
  return (
    <TouchableOpacity
      onPress={onPress}
      accessible={true}
      accessibilityRole="button"
      accessibilityLabel={label}
      accessibilityHint="Double tap to activate"
      // Web-specific ARIA
      {...(Platform.OS === 'web' && {
        'aria-label': label,
        role: 'button',
      })}
    >
      <Text>{label}</Text>
    </TouchableOpacity>
  );
}
```

## Deployment Checklist

### Pre-Deployment Validation

✅ **Test on all platforms**:
- [ ] iOS simulator (iPhone SE, iPhone 14, iPad)
- [ ] Android emulator (Pixel 4, Pixel 7, Tablet)
- [ ] Web browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge)
- [ ] Different screen sizes (phone, tablet, desktop)

✅ **Test responsive breakpoints**:
- [ ] Phone (375px)
- [ ] Tablet (768px)
- [ ] Desktop (1024px)
- [ ] Wide (1440px+)

✅ **Test platform-specific features**:
- [ ] Navigation works on all platforms
- [ ] Forms work with native keyboards
- [ ] Images load correctly
- [ ] Fonts render properly

✅ **Performance**:
- [ ] Web: Lighthouse score > 90
- [ ] Mobile: 60 FPS scrolling
- [ ] No memory leaks

✅ **PWA**:
- [ ] Installable on desktop
- [ ] Works offline
- [ ] Updates automatically

## Common Pitfalls to Avoid

### ❌ Don't: Use web-only libraries

```typescript
// ❌ BAD - react-router only works on web
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
```

### ✅ Do: Use Expo-compatible libraries

```typescript
// ✅ GOOD - react-navigation works everywhere
import { NavigationContainer } from '@react-navigation/native';
```

### ❌ Don't: Use fixed pixel values

```typescript
// ❌ BAD - Doesn't scale
<View style={{ width: 375 }} />
```

### ✅ Do: Use responsive percentages or flex

```typescript
// ✅ GOOD - Adapts to screen size
<View style={{ width: '100%', flex: 1 }} />
```

### ❌ Don't: Assume platform capabilities

```typescript
// ❌ BAD - Camera doesn't work on web
import { Camera } from 'expo-camera';
```

### ✅ Do: Check platform and provide fallbacks

```typescript
// ✅ GOOD - Fallback for web
if (Platform.OS === 'web') {
  // Use web file input
} else {
  // Use native camera
}
```

**Every app generated by the Design-First Software Factory follows these principles**:

1. ✅ **Built with Expo** (not generic React Native)
2. ✅ **Targets all platforms** (iOS, Android, Web)
3. ✅ **Mobile-first responsive design** (phone → tablet → desktop)
4. ✅ **Platform-aware styling** (adapts to iOS/Android/Web patterns)
5. ✅ **PWA capabilities** (installable, offline-capable)
6. ✅ **Comprehensive testing** (unit, component, E2E across platforms)
7. ✅ **Accessible** (WCAG compliant, screen reader support)
8. ✅ **Performant** (60 FPS, fast load times)

This ensures **universal accessibility**: users can access the app on their phone, tablet, or desktop browser with an optimal experience for each platform.
